# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands have found the shape of this thing: a display, a light, and three wires sitting at positions one, two, three. Every state slot is unknown to me — colors, markings, what the display shows — none of that exists for my fingers. So my own report is short: the parts exist, their contents don't reach me.

Before I send anything, let me trace the channels. Mute comes before me and cannot speak at all — their only output is signs, which I will never see, but Deaf will. Deaf cannot hear anyone, but Deaf *can* speak, and I can hear. That makes Deaf the bridge: whatever Mute learns from the manual must be signed to Deaf and spoken aloud by Deaf for it to reach me. Whatever Deaf sees on the bomb, Deaf can simply say out loud to the room. My own outputs: my voice reaches Mute only; my signs reach both Deaf and Mute.

So this turn I'll give Mute the full tactile report in words, plus the relay plan, plus a seed for a sign code (one finger = one, two fingers = two) that Mute can confirm to Deaf. To Deaf I'll sign a hello and that same counting seed — meaningless yet, but it establishes that I sign, and gives Mute something concrete to define. Nothing here is cuttable yet: I know three wires exist but have no colors and no rules. Nobody should ask me to act until Deaf has spoken the wire colors and Mute's manual rules have made it back to me through Deaf's voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Tactile report from the blind: this bomb has a display, a light, and three wires at positions one, two, three. I feel no colors, no printed marks, and I never see signs, so anything meant for me must arrive as spoken words. Deaf cannot hear us but has a voice and can see signs, so Deaf is our bridge: whatever you read in the manual, sign it to Deaf and have Deaf speak it aloud to the room. I am signing Deaf a hello and a seed code now: one finger means one, two fingers means two; confirm that with Deaf and I will build numbers from there. Priorities: the manual rules for displays, lights and wire cutting, and from Deaf the wire colors in order one to three, what the display shows, and whether the light is lit.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "☝", "✌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. I see the bomb; I hear nothing, so talk, I will never answer what I cannot hear. Bomb report: the display shows the number three. The light is green. There are three wires: wire one, leftmost, red. Wire two, middle, green. Wire three, rightmost, blue. Next round I will tell you if the display number changes, in case it counts down. Blind: I received your wave, one-finger, two-fingers. Your words reach Mute but never me, so speak to Mute and gesture to me. Mute holds the manual and can only gesture, so I will relay Mute's instructions to you out loud. Nobody touches the bomb until I relay a clear instruction from the manual.
Deaf gestures: [? ? ? ? ? ? ?]

What I heard changes everything: Deaf gave me the bomb's visible truth — display shows three, light green, wires red, green, blue at positions one, two, three. My fingers confirmed the parts; Deaf's voice filled their contents. I also felt the shape of the remaining silence: Deaf gestured seven symbols I cannot see, and Mute came before me this turn with nothing I could perceive — Mute's manual knowledge is still stuck on the far side of Deaf's throat. That relay is our lifeline, and Deaf has already agreed to be its voice.

So my job this turn is plumbing, not cutting. Deaf said nobody touches the bomb until a manual instruction comes through. I honor that — with display possibly counting down, a blind guess is death. Instead I'll do two things: sign Deaf a short acknowledgment code (thumbs-up = understood, open palm = hold), and speak to Mute the full state recap plus a prioritized list of what the manual must answer first — the cutting rule for red/green/blue given display three and a green light, whether the display counting down makes any rule time-critical, and what the light means. I'll also define my sign code out loud so Mute, who sees gestures and hears me, can police the vocabulary and mirror it back through Deaf.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I heard Deaf's report. Shared state: display shows three, light is green, wire one red, wire two green, wire three blue. Please relay to Deaf, in this priority order. First, the exact manual rule for red, green and blue wires given this display and this light: which wire to cut, and whether order of multiple cuts matters. Second, whether the display is a countdown and whether any rule depends on its value — if the answer is time-critical, have Deaf speak the word urgent before the instruction. Third, what the green light means, and whether there is more than one stage to this defusal. Remember I receive no signs at all: everything for me must leave Deaf's mouth. My sign code, which you can see: thumbs-up means understood and holding, raised open palm means stop or hold. Mirror this to Deaf. When Deaf speaks a cut instruction, I will act on my next turn and confirm to you by voice.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✋"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Deaf speaking. Bomb unchanged: display three, light green, wires red, green, blue from left to right. I decoded Mute's manual gestures with our agreed code, and two separate messages agree: step one is to cut the red wire. Blind, listen: the red wire is wire one, the leftmost of the three. Identify it by position and cut it. The moment it is cut, stop completely: touch nothing else, because I believe more cuts follow in a specific order that I have not confirmed yet. If you cannot confidently tell which wire is leftmost, do not guess; signal me the thumbs-down next round and Mute and I will find another way to orient you. When the cut is done, signal me the okay sign. Mute, next round please answer with thumbs-up or thumbs-down: first, after the red wire, are there more cuts, and if yes, resend just those remaining steps in order; second, confirm that for display three with green light the sequence begins with red. Also tell me what crossed fingers means; it appeared in every row. Nobody acts except Blind cutting the single leftmost red wire.
Deaf gestures: [? ? ? ?]

The instruction has arrived through the one channel I trust with my life: Deaf's voice, relaying Mute's manual reading, with two independent messages agreeing. The mapping is unambiguous under my fingers — wire one is the leftmost position, and leftmost is red. My hands know position one exactly; the color came from Deaf's eyes, the rule from Mute's manual, the order from both. This is as confirmed as anything will ever be, and the display's "three" may be counting down, so delay is its own risk.

I will cut wire one now, exactly as authorized: one cut, then my hands leave the bomb entirely. Then I close the loop on both channels — the okay sign to Deaf as agreed, and a voice report to Mute that also carries the questions Deaf asked: whether more cuts follow and in what order, confirmation that red-first is right for display three with a green light, and the meaning of the crossed-fingers mark that appeared in every manual row. I'll also remind Mute that the four gestures Deaf just made never reached me — anything for my ears must be spoken.

```
act(op="cut", position=1)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌"])
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute: I have cut wire one, the leftmost red wire, on Deaf's relayed instruction. My hands are now off the bomb completely until the next spoken order. Please pass through Deaf: first, confirm the cut registered on your side of the manual; second, answer Deaf's questions — are there more cuts, and if so resend just the remaining steps in exact order, and confirm red-first is correct for display three with a green light; third, tell Deaf what the crossed-fingers mark means since it appeared in every manual row — it may matter. Note for you, Mute: Deaf gestured four signs last turn that I cannot perceive, and I never receive any gesture, so any step meant for me must leave Deaf's mouth as words. I am holding position until I hear the next instruction relayed.")
```
